_owner: THE TEMPLATE'S PRIVACY NOTICE (TASK-L185). The one owner of its words AND its version. tools/build-privacy.mjs writes the `privacy` namespace into Data/Strings and the version into every cloud function that compares it; tools/check-privacy.mjs fails if any copy disagrees, if the deletion plan misses a collection, or if the text claims something the template does not do. It is NOT the product's notice: that one describes model calls, uploads, a connector and Google sign-in, none of which this template has. Change the words here, bump `version` when anything that matters changes, and run build-privacy.

privacy.title: Your data
privacy.lede: What this course holds about you, why, where it lives, and how to take it with you or get rid of it. It is short, and it is written to be read.

sections.heading: Your account
sections.body: Your email address, and your name if you or your coach gave one. There is no password. To sign in you ask for a link, and we email you one that works once and lasts fifteen minutes. Once you are in, that browser stays signed in until you sign out — there is no automatic time limit — so sign out on a computer you share. We also hold whether your account belongs to a coach. And whether you have asked us not to email you about messages, and when.

sections.heading: That you read this
sections.body: Which version of this notice you accepted, and when. If it changes, you are asked again before you carry on.

sections.heading: Your project
sections.body: What you are building, in your own words: its name, what it is for, and every answer you save from a lesson. Your coach sets it up with you, and each answer you save is added to it. Saving the same words twice changes nothing.

sections.heading: Your path, and how far along it you are
sections.body: The steps your coach chose for you, in order, with a sentence on why each one is there; which steps are open to you; and which you have finished, and when. Nothing here is a grade or a score.

sections.heading: Lessons written for you
sections.body: If a lesson has been written for your project, it is stored as yours alone. It is about your work, so it is personal data in the same way your project is.

sections.heading: Messages with your coach
sections.body: You can ask your coach about anything on your programme, and they can reply. We keep every message either of you writes, what on your programme it was about, when it was written, and whether the other person has opened it yet. Nothing you write to your coach is sent to an AI model. Your messages are in your download, and they are deleted with your account.

sections.heading: What is not here
sections.body: No notes about you, reviews or scores can be written in this version, nothing you do is sent to an AI model, and you cannot attach files. When any of that changes, this notice changes first and asks you again.

sections.heading: Who can see it
sections.body: You can see all of it, and download it whenever you like. Your coach can see your project, your path and how far along it you are, the answers you save, and the messages you write to them. Nobody else using the course can see any of it. The person who runs the service can reach the database to keep it working, and does not read it for anything else.

sections.heading: Why we hold it
sections.body: To run your course with your coach. That is the only reason. We do not sell it, share it with advertisers, or use it to build a profile of you.

sections.heading: Where it lives
sections.body: On one server we rent from Hetzner, in Falkenstein, Germany. One other company is involved: Brevo, an email service based in France, sends your sign-in links, so it sees your email address and the link. Nothing else leaves the server. The pages load nothing from anyone else's site.

sections.heading: Copies we keep in case something breaks
sections.body: Every night the server takes a copy of the database and keeps the last seven, on the same server. A copy holds everything above, as it was that night.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
sections.body: For as long as your account exists. When you delete it, it goes at once — apart from the nightly copies, which still hold it until they age out, within seven days. Brevo keeps its own record of the emails it sent you, under its own rules.

sections.heading: What you can do about it
sections.body: On your settings page you can download everything we hold about you as one file, and you can delete your account. Deleting is one action, with no support request and no waiting period, and it removes everything listed here. Nothing is kept afterwards, not even with your name taken off, because nothing here needs to be. Every email about a message has a link that stops them in one press, and a switch on your settings page does the same; neither stops your sign-in links.

sections.heading: Getting in touch
sections.body: Write to {{email}}. A person reads it. If you want your data, want it gone, or think something here is wrong, that is the address. If you are not happy with how we handled it, you have the right to complain to your national data-protection authority.

sections.heading: When this changes
sections.body: If anything that matters changes — a new kind of data, a new company handling it, a different period — the version at the top changes and you are asked to read it again before you carry on.

accept.title: Please read how we handle your data
accept.lede: This course has a privacy notice, and this version is new to you. It is short. Please read it and confirm you have.
accept.confirm: I have read it — carry on
accept.failed: That did not save. Please try again.
accept.settings: Rather not? Download or delete your account

settings.title: Your account
settings.lede: Sign out, take your data with you, or delete your account. None of this needs you to accept anything first.
settings.signOutBody: Ends this browser's session. You can sign in again with a new link.
settings.exportBody: Everything we hold about you, as one file. The top of the file says what it leaves out, if anything, and why.
settings.exportFailed: That did not work. Please try again.
settings.deleteBody: This removes your account and everything listed in the privacy notice: your project, your path, your progress, your answers and any lessons written for you. Nothing is kept with your name taken off. It cannot be undone. The nightly copies still hold it for up to seven days, and then it is gone from those too.
settings.deleteFailed: That did not finish. Your account is still here; please try again, and if it keeps happening, write to {{email}}.
settings.emailBody: When there is a new message for you on your course, we email you, with the message and a link to it. Turned off, you will only see new messages when you next open the course. Your sign-in links still arrive either way.
settings.emailFailed: That did not save. Please try again.

privacy.deleted: Your account has been deleted. Everything we held about you is gone.

unsubscribe.title: Stop emails about messages?
unsubscribe.body: This stops the emails we send when there is a new message for you on your course. Your sign-in links still arrive, because without them you could not get back in to turn these on again.
unsubscribe.done: Done. You will not get these emails again. You can turn them back on from your settings page.
unsubscribe.failed: That did not work. Please try again, or turn them off from your settings page.
unsubscribe.noLink: This link is not complete. Open the whole link from the email, or turn these emails off from your settings page.
